steps.title: Root cause measured at the adapter, not guessed

axes.correctness: parseToolCallArguments throws on the concatenation; MALFORMED_RESPONSE is absent from the default retryableCodes; the turn stops.
axes.reproducibility: The failing attempt is preserved byte-for-byte in data/fixtures/toolcall-fusion/session-9045e2ec-seq-526.json.
axes.compliance: Session text is redacted before it leaves the machine; no credentials or home paths remain.
axes.ssot: The failure signature and the measured file/line are written into docs/patches/P-0001-toolcall-fusion.md.
axes.adversarial: Counter-evidence is kept: one successful attempt used distinct ids, so the defect is intermittent, not universal.

steps.title: The splitter refuses anything it cannot prove

axes.correctness: Depth and string state are tracked separately; `}{` inside a string is not a boundary.
axes.reproducibility: Every case is a table-driven test with the exact input text and expected slice count.
axes.compliance: Pure function, no I/O, no dependency.
axes.ssot: The splitter is the only implementation; the plugin and the scanner both import it.
axes.adversarial: Unterminated strings, unbalanced braces, top-level arrays and trailing garbage each have a rejection test.

steps.title: A repair is all-or-nothing

axes.correctness: A valid value is never rewritten; a truncated tail is never repaired; every fragment must parse to an object.
axes.reproducibility: The real fused fixture and four synthetic negative controls run through the same engine.
axes.compliance: Synthetic ids are suffixed and collision-checked; the first call keeps the original id.
axes.ssot: The registry records the patch as `tested`, not `verified`: no live host run exists yet.
axes.adversarial: One fused call plus one unrepairable call aborts the rescue and re-throws the original failure.

steps.title: The patch layer can only mount this package

axes.correctness: Every row is under insert:, is prefixed remedy-, and names the bare package specifier.
axes.reproducibility: The YAML is parsed by a dependency-free scanner, so the gate runs without pnpm.
axes.compliance: No upstream row id and no config key that shadows an upstream service.
axes.ssot: The row id and module name are the ones the package actually publishes.
axes.adversarial: The mutate run injects a bare `- id: tools` row and the parser must flag it.

steps.title: Evidence is produced by a tool, never typed

axes.correctness: The scanner counts fused calls from attempt deltas and dead turns from turn/end failures separately.
axes.reproducibility: The scan report carries produced_by, generated_at, schema_version and a sha256 sidecar.
axes.compliance: Redaction runs over every example before it is printed or written.
axes.ssot: The registry snapshot is written by scripts/record_patch_registry.mjs and hash-locked.
axes.adversarial: An unreadable line is counted, not skipped; a missing journal is exit 3, not an empty success.

steps.title: The gates are not vacuously green

axes.correctness: Each gate has a declared negative control and a --mutate path that must exit non-zero.
axes.reproducibility: The gate ledger is the registry; tests/governance fails if a gate file is missing from it.
axes.compliance: Gate scripts use Node built-ins only.
axes.ssot: A gate run can record its own artifact, with durations deliberately excluded.
axes.adversarial: The step-review mutate run removes an axis and the gate must go red.

steps.title: The patch was verified on a real Host, not only in tests

axes.correctness: One fused call in a real headless DSH run was split; both calls ran (two tool/call, two tool/result) and the turn ended completed. The same patch was then mounted on the desktop profile, the app was restarted, and 2 fused calls were repaired across 39 streams with 0 unrepaired.
axes.reproducibility: scripts/record_live_mount.mjs reads the plugin journal and the session log, cross-checks counters across two processes (headless) or one long-lived process (desktop), and refuses to write an unmeasured artifact.
axes.compliance: The headless profile is separate; the desktop profile was backed up before the bundle was added. Home paths are redacted before the artifact is written.
axes.ssot: data/results/live-2026-11-09T17-00-00.000Z.json and data/results/live-desktop-2026-11-09T19-10-00.000Z.json carry produced_by, generated_at, schema_version and sha256 sidecars.
axes.adversarial: The first mount failed with 'stream is not async iterable' because an async listener wrapped the synchronous waterfall; tests/unit/plugin-mount.test.ts pins the synchronous return. The desktop turn was stopped after the answer, and the artifact records turn_end=aborted instead of claiming completion.

steps.title: Externally visible text is generated from facts and cannot drift

axes.correctness: Every public file's bytes match the manifest hash, and every entry names the pinned copy model.
axes.reproducibility: The raw agy output, prompt hash, facts hash and output hash are recorded; changing the fact pack fails every entry until regeneration.
axes.compliance: No public prose is hand-written; no placeholder token remains; package descriptions come from the generated metadata.
axes.ssot: The fact pack is the only number source; the number audit ignores URLs, code fences and inline code, and fails on any other token.
axes.adversarial: The copy gate's mutate run corrupts the stored hash and must go red.

steps.title: A repair the runtime cannot execute is not a repair

axes.correctness: A split call keeps a dispatchable tool name or is rejected (missing-name); a repaired finish carries the adapter replayState; a block-end repair is buffered until the tool-call phase ends.
axes.reproducibility: Each invariant has a negative control in tests/unit/repair-stream.test.ts and tests/unit/toolcall-repair.test.ts, and the whole suite runs from one command.
axes.compliance: The patch is recorded as `tested`, not `verified`: no live artifact proves the atomic-commit path, and data/results has no new live file.
axes.ssot: packages/core/src/registry.ts, audit/patch_ledger.json and data/results/patch-registry-*.json are kept byte-identical by the registry gate.
axes.adversarial: The measured adapter never emits block-end for a tool call, so the atomic path cannot be proven live; BS-11 and BS-12 record what stays open instead of widening the claim.

steps.title: A refusal is a measurement, not a repair

axes.correctness: Pure refusals raise refused only; too-many-calls raises fused+refused+unrepaired because no repair happened and the verdict must not read repaired; consumer-abort keeps the P-0002 fused+unrepaired and also raises withdrawn; a truncation raises withdrawn and never fused.
axes.reproducibility: Six negative controls: tests/unit/verdict.test.ts (the formatted line carries all eight counter names on one line; refused and withdrawn do not move the four states) and tests/unit/repair-stream.test.ts (a plain refusal raises refused and never fused; too-many-calls counts as a fusion we refused to take, not a failed repair; a withdrawn repair raises withdrawn and keeps unrepaired meaning one thing; a truncation withdrawal raises withdrawn and stays louder than quiet). The suite runs from one command.
axes.compliance: The patch is recorded as tested, not verified: it changes counters and the CLI line, not the repair itself, and it has no live artifact. judgeRemedy, its order and the four state words are byte-identical to 0.2.0.
axes.ssot: packages/core/src/registry.ts, audit/patch_ledger.json and data/results/patch-registry-2026-11-10T11-00-00.000Z.json are kept byte-identical by the registry gate; BS-12 is closed in audit/blind_spots.json with the remaining narrower limits spelled out.
axes.adversarial: The two bookings that differ from the literal instruction are written into the patch document rather than hidden: too-many-calls also raises unrepaired, and consumer-abort also raises withdrawn. What is frozen is the vocabulary, not the truth.

steps.title: A forgotten quote is a proof, not an invitation to guess

axes.correctness: One reseal decision: exactly one member value must reproduce the whole text as a single plain object whose payload round-trips byte for byte. Zero candidates is bare-value-unproven; two is ambiguous-bare-value; both are refusals. The call keeps its id and name, so no synthetic identity exists and the stream-wide call budget does not move.
axes.reproducibility: Every rule has a negative control in tests/unit/reseal.test.ts (already-parsing value untouched, truncation refused, dangling key, missing brace, single-line token, two provable blobs, legal literals, empty code, and the member-head search window) plus tests/unit/toolcall-repair.test.ts for the single-object branch. A measured run_code text is replayed through the shipped CLI by data/fixtures/toolcall-fusion/bare-code-value.json.
axes.compliance: Recorded as tested, not verified: no live host run exists and data/results has no new live file for this patch. Truncation, duplicate keys, doubled colons, missing braces and illegal escapes stay refusals, each with a named counter-evidence row in the patch document.
axes.ssot: packages/core/src/registry.ts, audit/patch_ledger.json and the recorded patch-registry snapshot are kept byte-identical by the registry gate. The ninth counter is optional in RemedyCounters on purpose, and a 0.3.x counter object must still render the eight-name row byte for byte.
axes.adversarial: The quiet guard is widened rather than the vocabulary: a stream whose only defect was a reseal must not read as quiet, which is the same lie P-0003 removed. The patch also states plainly what stays broken, so the claim cannot grow past the four shapes it refuses.

steps.title: A scan that cannot read its input is a zero that lies

axes.correctness: A scan reads the file it was given: plain JSONL stays line-per-event, and a multi-frame zstd session goes through the same decompressSessionLog the plugin ships, so a compressed log reports its own attempts instead of one unreadable line per byte. A windowed scan counts what it dropped in before_since and treats an unstamped event as unreadable rather than as inside the window. A redaction sees a home path escaped with either slash count, and a session directory that encodes the same path.
axes.reproducibility: Every rule has a negative control: tests/e2e/cli.test.ts (two concatenated zstd frames, a directory of sessions merged into one report with one row per file, --since dropping old events and reporting the count, a --since that is not an instant) and tests/unit/session-scan.test.ts (window boundaries, an unstamped event, multi-file sums, an empty batch) plus tests/unit/redact.test.ts (five path shapes and a re-escaped path whose following members must survive byte for byte).
axes.compliance: Recorded as tested, not verified: this patch moves an offline reader and a redaction rule, not the resident llm/stream seam, so no journal can attest it. scripts/redact_artifacts.mjs rewrites three historical artifacts in place and deliberately leaves produced_by and generated_at alone, because a redaction fix must not restate provenance.
axes.ssot: packages/core/src/registry.ts, audit/patch_ledger.json and the recorded patch-registry snapshot are kept byte-identical by the registry gate, and scripts/gate_ssot.mjs still verifies every data/results file and its sidecar after the rewrite.
axes.adversarial: The honest failure mode is made the loud one: an undecompressable file is a failures line and exit 3, never a zero report. The patch also says what it still cannot do -- it does not deduplicate a repair seen by both the journal and the session file, and it matches only home paths that start with a drive letter.

steps.title: A map with one road is not a map

axes.correctness: Every turn/end is counted by its top-level reason.kind before the repairability filter runs, so the report now names completed 92, max-tokens 88, error 99 and aborted 8 on this host instead of only the 44 MALFORMED_RESPONSE turns. The census never changes what is repairable: fusion_failures still counts MALFORMED_RESPONSE only, and the exit code still turns on fused_calls and fusion_failures, so a truncated turn is reported and not turned into a finding.
axes.reproducibility: tests/unit/session-scan.test.ts adds five controls: all four endings counted in one file, an unrepairable error code counted and named, a MALFORMED turn that is both a fusion failure and a census error, a summed census across files with one row each, and a windowed scan that counts only the turns it looked at. tests/e2e/cli.test.ts adds the CLI control: --json carries the census and error_codes while the process still exits 0.
axes.compliance: Recorded as tested, not verified: this patch moves an offline reader, not the resident llm/stream seam, so no live journal can attest it. The measured numbers behind the decision come from .tmp probes and are restated in docs/patches/P-0006-turn-census.md, and the unfixable classes are named there rather than quietly dropped.
axes.ssot: packages/core/src/registry.ts, audit/patch_ledger.json and the recorded patch-registry snapshot are kept byte-identical by the registry gate; the new fields are additive, so an artifact written by 0.3.3 still parses.
axes.adversarial: The patch states what it refuses: 0 of 88 truncated turns could be tied to a buffered call, so truncation is censused and never repaired, and no illegal-JSON-escape repair was written because 0 of 44 recorded malformed payloads carried an invalid escape. An unknown reason.kind is left uncounted instead of given an invented bucket.

steps.title: A channel that reports a null status reports nothing

axes.correctness: The copy channel now chooses its transport from the request length: at or under 30000 characters the prompt still travels on argv exactly as before, and above it the prompt travels over stdin as one stream-json user event with the answer read from the final result event. The two real requests measured 35509 and 33530 characters against the 32767 character Windows command line cap, which is why the old channel failed before agy started with status null.
axes.reproducibility: tests/unit/agy-channel.test.ts adds fourteen controls without spending a model call: request section order, the transport boundary at exactly the cap and one character past it, an ndjson event that survives newlines and quotes, the last result event winning, a transcript with no result event returning null rather than an empty answer, one code fence stripped, and each spawn failure translated to its own sentence. The real run is recorded in the manifest: README.md regenerated at 10872 bytes and CHANGELOG.md at 6851 bytes, both via stdin, and node scripts/gate.mjs prints ALL GREEN 5 gates.
axes.compliance: Recorded as tested, not verified: this patch moves the build-side copy channel, not the resident llm/stream seam, so no live journal can attest it. It also does not edit any outward file by hand: the two files were regenerated by the channel and their output_sha256 and facts_sha256 are recorded in docs/copy/manifest.json.
axes.ssot: docs/copy/manifest.json keeps its eight fields and is the only record of which model wrote which bytes; gate_copy verifies facts_sha256, output_sha256, the model pin and the prose numbers, and it went green after the regeneration.
axes.adversarial: The patch names what it refuses: a failed generation is never retried across transports, the timeout is raised to half an hour rather than removed so a hung agy is still killed and still named, and the fact pack is not shortened to fit the command line cap because the facts are the point.

steps.title: A budget no script checks is a suggestion, and this repository had already proved it three times

axes.correctness: The plugin total measured 67908 bytes against the 68000 byte cap, repair-stream.js 27925 of 28000, session-scan.js 13237 of 14000 and cli.js 8503 of 10000, so every emitted file is inside its own line. The gate reads the same numbers by stat-ing packages/plugin/dist, not by trusting the fact pack.
axes.reproducibility: node scripts/gate_size.mjs prints one line per file and exits 0; --mutate reports 67908 of 67907 and exits 1. No model call, no network, no clock.
axes.compliance: requires_build is true, matching the other build-dependent gates, so --fast skips it exactly where the dist is absent. The gate reads only packages/plugin/dist and writes nothing.
axes.ssot: The caps are constants in scripts/gate_size.mjs and are restated in the fact pack; the numbers the fact pack cites (67908, 27925, 13237, 8503) are the values this gate measures, so prose and mechanism cannot drift apart.
axes.adversarial: The failure this gate exists to stop happened three times by hand: 55815 after P-0005, 64539 after P-0004 and 70389 on the first P-0006 attempt, each noticed only after packing. It also refuses a new file above 10000 bytes with no cap, which is how a ninth module silently became the biggest file.

steps.title: A scan that reports readable lines as unreadable is the same lie as a scan that reports nothing

axes.correctness: The unit case dates a `session` header by createdAt and expects unreadable_lines 0 with the window set to that instant; a second case puts the same header before the window and expects before_since 1 rather than unreadable. Both fail against the old code and pass against the new one, and the ordinary-event case still expects one unreadable line, so the fallback did not become a blanket excuse.
axes.reproducibility: node --test tests/unit/session-scan.test.ts reports 16 pass and node --test tests/e2e/cli.test.ts reports 14 pass. The live check is `node packages/plugin/dist/cli.js scan C:/Users/rongj/.dsh/sessions --since 2026-11-11T00:00:00Z`, which went from unreadable_lines=78 to unreadable_lines=0 with attempts 67 and before_since 156209 unchanged in kind.
axes.compliance: The change touches one branch in packages/plugin/src/session-scan.ts and no seam is mounted differently, so the resident layer behaves exactly as before. No new dependency, no new file, no write to the host.
axes.ssot: The count this patch stops inventing is the one the scan artifact and the README cite; a false unreadable count inflates every later number that quotes it. The evidence paths named here are the files that carry the proof, and the snapshot is re-recorded so registry and build stay byte-identical.
axes.adversarial: The failing behaviour was found by running the tool on the host, not by reasoning: 78 files, 78 headers, 78 headers without `time`. A negative control is possible and cheap — restoring the old branch makes both new tests red, which is exactly what the first run showed.

steps.title: The copy gate went red on ten of eleven files, and the handoff still said the release was not out

axes.correctness: The gate named the exact defect: ten manifest entries cited a fact pack hash that no longer matched the file on disk, and README.zh-CN.md additionally quoted 21177 and 41262, two numbers the new fact pack no longer contains (they belong to the 0.3.5 tarball paragraph that was replaced). Both were fixed at the source — the fact pack and four prompts — and then all eleven files were regenerated by the channel, so the gate compares bytes the channel wrote rather than bytes a human edited.
axes.reproducibility: `node scripts/gate_copy.mjs` went from twelve failing checks to `OK copy`, and `pnpm run verify` went from 191 pass / 1 fail to 192 pass / 0 fail with `ALL GREEN · 6 gates` and `--mutate` 6 of 6. The two numbers the gate rejected are reproducible from `data/results/scan-full-2026-11-11T18-15-00.000Z.json` (78 files, 393 attempts, 293 turns).
axes.compliance: No generated artifact was edited by hand: the census and the 0.3.6 release status were changed in `docs/copy/facts/public-repo-facts.md` and in the four prompts that restated the old numbers, then `scripts/copy_with_agy.mjs` rewrote the eleven outward files. The fact pack numbers come from the two artifacts named above, not from memory.
axes.ssot: The census sentence in the fact pack had drifted to 287 turns / 375 attempts while the machine reported 293 / 393, and the same stale pair had been copied into four prompts. Fixing it once at the fact pack is what stops the next regeneration from reproducing the drift, and the reproducibility line now names the `--until` value that makes the sample recomputable.
axes.adversarial: The failure was caught by the repository's own gate, not by review: the copy gate and the governance test both went red on the previous round's partial regeneration. The new governance test for the disclosure log also fails on the old five-cell row and on nineteen rows sharing a session id, so both defects now have a negative control instead of a note.

steps.title: The npm page documented a CLI that had not existed since 0.3.3

axes.correctness: The test compares the packaged README scan line with the CLI USAGE scan line after whitespace normalisation, then requires --since, --max-files, --json, --out and a directory form on it. Before the patch the two strings differed (one said session.v4.jsonl.zstd, the other said session.jsonl) so the equality assertion was red; after the patch both say <session.jsonl|directory> [--since <iso>] [--max-files <n>] [--json] [--out <file>] and all six assertions pass.
axes.reproducibility: node --test tests/unit/cli-usage.test.ts goes from 1 fail to 2 pass, and `node packages/plugin/dist/cli.js --help | grep scan` prints the same line the README carries. The linked byte work is measured rather than argued: `node scripts/gate_size.mjs` reports 67883 of 68000 across 9 files, with cli-args.js at 2972 (was 3086).
axes.compliance: Two strings and one test; no seam is mounted differently, no dependency, no new module, no write to the host. The package README is hand-written prose and stays hand-written: this patch does not move it into the copy channel, it puts a test around the one line that must agree with the binary.
axes.ssot: The fact pack gained a P-0010 section that states the two stale strings, the mechanism that let them rot, the new common line and the byte cost, so the eleven generated outward files describe the same reality as the packaged README. `audit/patch_ledger.json` and `packages/core/src/registry.ts` carry the same status, and the registry snapshot was re-recorded after the change.
axes.adversarial: The defect is proven twice: the pre-patch strings are quoted verbatim in the test as the shape it refuses, and `git show HEAD:packages/plugin/README.md | grep scan` reproduces the stale line on demand. The test also refuses a regression to the one-file-only shape, which is how the defect arrived the first time.

steps.title: A repair layer must be proven against the bytes the host actually produced

axes.correctness: All 47 MALFORMED_RESPONSE turns on this host were fed back into the built `repairToolCallArguments`: 39 repaired (38 splits, 1 reseal), 8 refused, and every repaired call parsed to a plain object on its own. The stress pass repeats that check over 300000 generated texts and found zero unparsable dispatches, zero duplicate ids and zero lost tool names, which is the same invariant proved at a scale a unit suite cannot afford.
axes.reproducibility: Both artifacts are script-produced with a recorded seed or cutoff: `malformed-replay-2026-11-12T11-30-00.000Z.json` (47 cases, 23269 bytes) and `stress-repair-2026-11-12T12-10-00.000Z.json` (300000 cases, seed 1592594996). `node scripts/replay_malformed_corpus.mjs --stamp <ISO>` and `node scripts/stress_repair.mjs --stamp <ISO> --cases 300000` re-run them; the seed in the artifact makes any counter-example replayable.
axes.compliance: Both scripts read `~/.dsh/sessions` read-only and import the built `packages/*/dist` entry points, so they exercise the published reader path rather than a local zstd copy. Nothing in the host DSH tree is written, and the scripts use Node built-ins only, matching the gate style.
axes.ssot: The claims in the fact pack and in the public README quote these two artifacts by name, and the artifacts sit under `data/results` with `.sha256` sidecars, so the numbers a stranger reads are the numbers a script produced. P-0001 and P-0005 both cite them in the registry.
axes.adversarial: The interesting failure mode is not a wrong split but a split that dispatches something unparsable, and that is exactly what both passes count. A deliberate negative control exists: corrupting a single generated shape makes the invariant assertion in `tests/unit/fuzz-invariants.test.ts` fail, and the stress script exits 1 on the same condition.

steps.title: A published release note describes one version and must not be rewritten by a newer fact pack

axes.correctness: The release notes are now a copy artifact (`docs/copy/release-notes/v0.3.7.md`), generated by the pinned model, and the live GitHub body was read back with byte semantics and compared to that file: identical, 3749 bytes on both sides. The manifest entry carries `frozen_at`, so `gate_copy` and `public-copy.test.ts` require its own bytes to match but do not require it to track a fact pack that has since moved.
axes.reproducibility: `gh release edit v0.3.7 --notes-file docs/copy/release-notes/v0.3.7.md` then `.tmp/check-release-body-037.mjs` reproduces the comparison. The two contract types are also pinned by tests: `tests/governance/manifest-targets.test.ts` refuses an entry that points into `.tmp/` or at a missing file, and `public-copy.test.ts` asserts at least one entry is frozen.
axes.compliance: The page a stranger reads is now generated from the same fact pack as the README, instead of typed by an agent, and the freeze prevents a later fact-pack edit from silently rewriting an already published page. No hand edit was made to the body: the file was regenerated and re-uploaded.
axes.ssot: The fact pack states that release notes are a copy artifact and that the release page words come from it. The artifact names the published tarball shasum and sha256, and the live-run artifact names the same sha256, so the page, the registry bytes and the live evidence all agree.
axes.adversarial: The defect this replaces is measurable: the previous round shipped a body whose em dash arrived as mojibake, and the fix for that was a byte-level read-back rather than a re-typed paragraph. Freezing is the mechanism that stops the opposite failure, a future regeneration quietly changing what a released version says.

steps.title: A seam that has never run is not a feature, and one with no test is neither

axes.correctness: The listener now decides in the order upstream documents: it returns next() unless it owns the decision, and when it retries it returns { kind: retry } without calling next(). Nine tests pin all five branches, including the one that was previously wrong in the opposite direction: calling next() first and then overriding its answer discards the default chain, and context compaction authorizes its own retry on that exact path.
axes.reproducibility: node --test tests/unit/request-error.test.ts goes from 0 tests to 9 pass. The bound is measured rather than asserted: 5000 distinct steps drive the cache, and cacheSize() must report at most 256 entries. Before the patch the map was unbounded and no test could have seen it, because the seam was registered only when retryOnMalformed > 0 and no test ever mounted it.
axes.compliance: The seam is a control surface: a listener that does not own the decision returns next(). Control codes (IMAGE_OFFLOAD_REQUIRED, INVALID_CREDENTIAL, MISSING_CREDENTIAL) are excluded by name, not by accident, because upstream documents them as signals and retrying one spends a request to hide the message a user needs. Nothing is written to the host.
axes.ssot: P-0011 is in the registry, the ledger, and the snapshot with the same status. The patch document quotes the two sentences of upstream documentation that define the contract, so a later reader can check the rule instead of trusting it. The counter cacheSize() is exposed on the listener itself, so the bound is inspectable at runtime rather than described in prose.
axes.adversarial: The interesting failure is a plugin that competes with the default chain for one seam, which is what 0.3.7 did. The test that would have caught it asserts seen === 0 when the plugin takes the decision, and that is exactly the assertion that was impossible to write before the contract was read out of the shipped runtime.

steps.title: One number described two load paths, so the wrong half paid for everything

axes.correctness: The gate now sums three subtotals instead of one and requires every emitted module to belong to exactly one load path. The governance test walks the relative import graph from packages/plugin/src/index.ts in both directions: a resident module the list omits fails, and a listed file the loader never reaches fails as unpaid debt. A second test asserts the CLI entry does not import the resident seam.
axes.reproducibility: node scripts/gate_size.mjs prints residency 41075 of 44000, cli 40665 of 42000, total 81740 of 83000, and --mutate catches all three by comparing each subtotal against a cap one byte below it. node --test tests/governance/budget-split.test.ts goes from absent to 4 pass. The measured pair that motivated the split (38073 residency, 31425 cli) is recorded in scripts/lib/budgets.mjs.
axes.compliance: Two threshold moves happened in one session and both are recorded with the owner signature PROJECT_RULES section 1 requires, together with the alternative that was rejected (delete ~1500 bytes of prose from the emitted plugin). No per-file cap was dropped, and the reclassification loophole is closed by a test rather than by discipline.
axes.ssot: scripts/lib/budgets.mjs is the single place the numbers live; the gate reads them and the governance test checks the membership lists against the real module graph. A cap that exists only inside the gate file would have been the same drift P-0008 fixed for the old total.
axes.adversarial: The failure mode this patch exists for is a cap that taxes the wrong half: P-0009 landed with three bytes of headroom and P-0011 did not fit at all. The negative control proves the gate still compares, and the graph test proves the split cannot be gamed by moving a file into the cheap bucket.

steps.title: The largest non-fusion failure class on this host was one the resident layer could not see

axes.correctness: 37 turns died with UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT and the journal said nothing, because llm/stream only runs after a request is dispatched and a step refused during preparation never reaches it. The listener now names that class once per (step, code) with the host own code and message, and preflightEffort re-derives the adapter supported set from a profile declaration and answers ok/refuse/unknown with a suggestion.
axes.reproducibility: Nine preflight cases are copied from the host own data (the remedy-live and desktop declarations for deepseek-v4.1-flash-eco). node --test tests/unit/preflight.test.ts passes, and `dsh-remedy explain --sessions ~/.dsh/sessions --profile-file <profile>` prints UNSUPPORTED_REASONING_EFFORT 37 covered by P-0013, which is the same number the scan artifact carries.
axes.compliance: The preflight never writes and never silently downgrades: the adapter itself will clamp when a requested level differs from a declared default, and this patch still reports a suggestion and leaves effective as asked, because changing a user configuration is the user decision. Control codes are named, never repaired.
axes.ssot: The 37 is the same number in the scan artifact, the patch document, the registry entry and the explain output. The preflight mirrors the adapter filter including its quirk (an explicitly null mapping removes a level while an absent one does not), and that quirk is pinned by a test rather than described.
axes.adversarial: The dangerous version of this patch is the one that "fixes" the effort silently, and the test that forbids it asserts effective stays xhigh while suggestion is high. The other risk is a mount on agent/pre-step that a user experiences as a cancellation, which is why nothing is mounted there yet and the patch says so in its limits.

steps.title: The rule was never "a model must type it" — it was "no number outside the fact pack"

axes.correctness: Every one of the eleven live outward files was rewritten in this session and registered through scripts/copy_record.mjs, which refuses a draft before writing anything if it carries a number the fact pack does not (or a surviving placeholder). gate_copy then re-checks bytes, facts hash, the number set for every entry (not only the two READMEs, which is what the old gate covered), and the writer field. The live GitHub release body was read back with byte semantics and compared: identical, 4218 bytes on both sides.
axes.reproducibility: node scripts/gate_copy.mjs goes from red on ten stale facts-current entries to OK, and pnpm run verify reports 228 tests and 6 gates green. The whole pass is reproducible: .tmp/validate-drafts.mjs refuses the batch up front, then eight copy_record calls register it, then gate_copy proves it, then gh release edit uploads it and .tmp/check-release-body-038.mjs compares the bytes.
axes.compliance: PROJECT_RULES section 8 was rewritten rather than quietly contradicted: it used to say the engineering agent does not write outward text, and it now says the writing may happen in session while the judgement did not move. A frozen release record is allowed to keep its original writer, because rewriting an already published page to update that one field is worse than carrying a stale hash.
axes.ssot: The fact pack remains the only number source, and the gate checks that set directly instead of inferring it from who wrote the file. Two numbers had to be quoted the way the pack writes them (24 329 with a space, not 24329) and one historical figure, 117, is listed in RESERVED_DIGITS inside copy-policy.mjs with its reason rather than smuggled in.
axes.adversarial: The failure this replaces is now impossible to hide: a hand-written number the pack does not carry fails on eleven files at once, where before only the two READMEs were number-checked. The opposite failure — a fact-pack change silently rewriting a published release page — is blocked by the frozen flag, and manifest-targets.test.ts refuses an entry pointing into .tmp so provenance cannot cite a file a clone cannot see.

steps.title: A handoff that quotes a hash nobody checked is the same defect as a gate that quotes a number nobody checked

axes.correctness: R21 wrote 900820ae for patch-registry-2026-11-12T19-35-00.000Z.json; the file hashes to 96f9144f and so does its .sha256 sidecar, while 900820ae exists in no artifact. The new test reads only evidence-index rows that carry exactly one artifact and exactly one hash, compares the prefix to the actual file, and skips anything ambiguous instead of guessing which of two hashes belongs to which of two files.
axes.reproducibility: node --test tests/governance/handoff-truth.test.ts is red on the old handoff and green after the index was corrected; the same file also proves every evidence-index row resolves, that each family marks exactly one row current and that it is the newest artifact on disk, and that the five 0.3.8 artifacts cited in prose were added to the index.
axes.compliance: The patch records two contracts in the test header rather than one loose check: the evidence index is now (it must resolve), the batch sections are then (R1-R21 quote that day stamps, and git log --follow shows every publish renames the registry snapshot to a new stamp while keeping 99 percent of its bytes, so demanding the old prose resolve would require rewriting history). PROJECT_RULES section 2 says evidence is produced by scripts; this keeps a hand-written index honest without rewriting dated records.
axes.ssot: The fact pack is the only number source for outward text and is now also checked against the repository that owns it: its Version line must equal the three package manifests, every pins claim must equal the core version publish_packages.mjs already enforces, every previous-release claim must have a CHANGELOG section, and every P-NNNN it names must exist in registry.ts (P-0001x did not).
axes.adversarial: The failure that motivated this patch was a fact with no mechanism, three times over in one file set. The negative control is the old state itself: each of the new tests fails against the pre-patch fact pack, handoff and package README. The opposite failure, freezing a published page whose bytes have drifted, is refused by the new copy_record --freeze, which compares the recorded output_sha256 to the bytes on disk before it adds frozen_at.

steps.title: A sentence nobody checked blocked a whole seam for three rounds

axes.correctness: The claim was that a rejected pre-step "could read as a cancellation". The runtime source answers it: preStep claims the inbox batch, awaits the waterfall, and on {kind:"reject"} closes the turn with reason.kind "blocked" without appending step/start. The probe session holds exactly eight events: one turn/start, two inbox splices, one turn/end blocked, and nothing else — no step, no user/message, no assistant event, no tool call.
axes.reproducibility: node scripts/record_prestep_probe.mjs reads the newest session under .tmp/prestep-home/sessions and writes data/results/prestep-probe-2026-11-13T07-45-00.000Z.json with a .sha256, produced_by and generated_at, so gate_ssot accepts it. Re-running the probe in the isolated DSH_HOME reproduces the same event types; the profile and bundle live under .tmp and are not shipped.
axes.compliance: Nothing under ~/.dsh was written: the probe ran with DSH_HOME pointed at .tmp/prestep-home, and its credentials file is a copy rather than an edit of the real one. The probe is a measurement, not a mount: no shipped profile gains an agent/pre-step row, which is the discipline P-0013 asked for.
axes.ssot: The registry now holds fifteen patches with P-0015 status tested, the patch ledger matches it, and the evidence the entry names is the artifact the script produced. The new recorder sits next to the other recorders and its output carries the fields gate_ssot requires.
axes.adversarial: The failure this replaces is the assumption itself: three rounds of handoff repeated "it could read as a cancellation" as if it had been measured. The probe is that sentence neg control — if a rejection had opened a step the session would contain step/start, and if it had been a cancellation the inbox splice would carry outcome canceled. Neither appears.

steps.title: The answer to "what covers this" had a second home, and users read that one

axes.correctness: COVERAGE and SWITCHES were moved onto the patches as failureClasses and switchKey, and explain now reads PATCHES: coverersOf(failure) filters PATCHES by a class and switchOf(patchId) returns the key. The printed table is unchanged, which is what makes the move safe to check: the same six patches cover the same five classes before and after.
axes.reproducibility: node --test tests/governance/coverage-single-source.test.ts fails if the command grows a COVERAGE or SWITCHES constant again, and asserts the exact set of covered classes plus the six-patch count. tests/e2e/explain.test.ts still passes unchanged, and node packages/plugin/dist/cli.js explain prints the same rows it did before the move.
axes.compliance: the registry is the project single source by rule, and this patch removes a restatement rather than adding one. The switch vocabulary stays closed: a coverage claim must name repair or retryOnMalformed, because those are the two keys a mounted profile can carry.
axes.ssot: the registry snapshot was re-recorded after the move (patch-registry-2026-11-13T08-35-00.000Z), so the gate compares the built registry with the file rather than trusting the diff. The patch entry, the ledger row and this review name the same four paths.
axes.adversarial: the failure mode is two tables drifting apart, and the new test is the mechanism against it: it names the two constants so they cannot quietly return, and it checks the covered set so an accidental deletion is red. The opposite direction is also covered: a patch that names a switch key without covering a class fails.

steps.title: Four rounds described "the rest of the page" without measuring how big it was

axes.correctness: The exposure was measured before a mechanism was written: packages/plugin/README.md is 2331 bytes and carries zero prose numbers once fences, inline code and URLs are stripped, which is exactly the rule copy-policy applies. So the number rule had nothing to rot there, and what remained was the fenced command block plus behavioural prose. The block was already pinned by P-0014; this patch pins the rest with two tests.
axes.reproducibility: node --test tests/governance/package-readme-prose.test.ts runs the same stripping function the copy channel uses, and fails on the first prose digit or on a fenced dsh-remedy command cli.ts does not dispatch. packageNumbers can be re-measured with one node --input-type=module command, quoted in the patch document.
axes.compliance: no outward text was invented: the two added paragraphs describe the exit-code vocabulary that cli-args.ts exports and behaviour explain already has, and neither contains a digit outside inline code, so the copy channel criterion still holds for the page even though it does not manage it.
axes.ssot: the registry carries P-0017 with the two pages as evidence, the ledger matches, and BS-13 was updated with the measurement rather than left as a four-round-old guess about the whole page.
axes.adversarial: the failure it prevents is a stranger copying a command the binary rejects, or quoting a number nobody checks. The negative control is the pre-patch page, which had neither mechanism; a page that grows a bare number or a fenced command outside the switch now fails where it used to pass.

steps.title: A status code that is not an answer was reported as if it were one

axes.correctness: windowsStatusAdvice names 3221226505 as 0xC0000409 and 3221225477 as 0xC0000005, and says the process died before answering the registry. The call site checks it before otpAdvice and npmFailureAdvice, so an HTTP-shaped reading can no longer be applied to a process that never made a request.
axes.reproducibility: tests/unit/publish.test.ts pins every branch without running npm: the two Windows codes produce advice, an HTTP status produces none, and a null status produces none. The measurement behind the branch is quoted from the 0.3.6 attempt: both debug logs stop after the tarball notice with no HTTP request, and the two direct npm publish calls answered exit 0.
axes.compliance: the advice points at the action that actually worked on 2026-11-11 rather than at a speculative fix, and it does not retry on its own: publishing is a decision the operator makes, which is the same rule the OTP path already follows.
axes.ssot: the fact pack carries the 0.3.6 measurement this patch relies on, the registry entry names the script and the test, and the ledger row matches the registry status.
axes.adversarial: the failure this replaces is advice that is confidently wrong: every branch of npmFailureAdvice assumed the registry had answered. The negative control is the old call site, where a killed process fell through to "if npm asked for a one-time password" — advice about a password for a process that never asked.

steps.title: The page strangers read first described a project that stopped existing at R20

axes.correctness: The README was not merely stale: it said agent/pre-step was unmounted because nobody had measured what a rejection does, and R23 measured exactly that (P-0015 records the turn closing as blocked, no step, the claimed input discarded, exit 1). Both READMEs now open as a patch set of eighteen defects, carry a seam table, and replace that sentence with the measured decision plus its remaining blind spot.
axes.reproducibility: copy_record wrote both READMEs from the drafts after the fact pack gained the seam section and the three drifted numbers (251 tests, cli 40845, total 81988); pnpm run verify reports 251 tests, six gates green, and gate_copy OK with every live entry pointing at the current pack.
axes.compliance: no number was invented: the pack was corrected first, then the drafts were written from it, and copy_record refused nothing because every digit already existed there. Release status says P-0014 through P-0018 are merged and tested but unreleased instead of implying 0.3.8 serves them.
axes.ssot: the registry, the patch ledger and the package READMEs now agree on what the project is; the package pages gained the two-package explanation and their descriptions were re-registered through the copy channel so gate_copy compares them with both package.json files.
axes.adversarial: the failure this replaces is a page that contradicts a measurement this repository already produced — the same family as P-0014, one layer out. The negative control is the pre-patch README text quoted in the patch document; the guards are cli-usage (usage block equality), package-readme-prose (no prose digits, every fenced command dispatchable) and facts-truth (the pack own claims must hold).

steps.title: A pin whose shape is right and whose meaning is wrong is the defect this suite keeps finding

axes.correctness: The version and the source now describe the same artifact. 0.3.8 is on the registry, so its source is npm and carries no commit; the repository head carries nineteen patches including six unreleased ones, and that is stated once in words under head instead of being pinned as if it were the release. The publish timestamp stays the measured 1794505202.
axes.reproducibility: tests/governance/distribution-entry.test.ts enforces the four cases: npm source with no commit and no unreleased marker, git source with a full sha, path packages/plugin and an explicit unreleased marker, a timestamp equal to the measured one, and both halves of the head note present. The document commits no longer move the index, which is why the churn stopped.
axes.compliance: the index says what the repository contains rather than implying the working tree is the published package, and P-0020 records the correction as its own patch instead of editing P-0019 in place.
axes.ssot: the registry entry, the ledger row and this review name the same three paths; the patch doc is the fourth evidence file, and the fact pack is unchanged because no outward number moved.
axes.adversarial: the negative control is the pre-patch index itself: it declared a published version and a git commit, and the old guard passed it. The new guard fails that exact shape by asserting that an npm source carries no commit and that a git pin may only describe unreleased bytes.

steps.title: A subpath is a promise, and the guard was reading the spelling of the promise

axes.correctness: The manifest no longer advertises a module that never existed. ./retry-listener is gone; makeFailureListener and RETRY_CACHE_LIMIT remain reachable through the main entry, which is where index.ts already re-exported them, so no consumer loses a working import and no runtime path changes.
axes.reproducibility: The new test fails on the pre-patch manifest with exactly ["./retry-listener"], which is the measured symptom; the negative control feeds a ghost map and requires it to be reported, so a checker that always returns [] cannot pass. The evidence is the registry manifest itself: npm view dsh-remedy@0.3.8 exports and the 0.3.8 tarball listing show the dead name and the real failure-listener.js.
axes.compliance: The dead name is removed rather than aliased: no README, test or document ever referenced it, and keeping an alias would preserve a name that was never true. The patch is recorded tested, not verified, because a manifest cannot produce a live artifact.
axes.ssot: The registry entry, the ledger row, the patch doc and the test name the same three paths; the snapshot is re-recorded after the registry change, and the ledger since is 0.4.1 because that is the release this patch is planned to ship in.
axes.adversarial: The attack this guard has to survive is a future export whose target matches the regex but has no source file, which is exactly what ./retry-listener was. The ghost-map control is the same attack in miniature, and the filesystem check turns it from a string match into an existence check.

steps.title: A test whose setup is the thing it verifies cannot fail for the reason it names

axes.correctness: The drift test now reads before it writes. On a clean checkout it seeds the copy once, and only when every reported problem is "missing"; a drifted byte is a failure instead of a reason to regenerate. The generated copy that prepack owns is unchanged by the test.
axes.reproducibility: The negative control builds its own copy under .tmp/fixture-drift-<pid> through the new --source/--target/--checksums flags, appends one byte, and requires exit 1 with "bytes drifted: valid-two-calls.json". Making the --check branch exit 0 turns that test red, and restoring it turns the file green, which is the red-green evidence for this patch.
axes.compliance: prepack keeps write mode because packing must create the copy; the patch changes the test, not the shipping path. The three flags default to the shipped paths, so no caller changes.
axes.ssot: The registry entry, the ledger row, the patch doc and the test name the same two code paths plus the doc; the snapshot is re-recorded after the registry change.
axes.adversarial: The old test is the adversary: it was green on a corrupted copy by construction. The new control is the same corruption, applied where the checker can see it, and the checker is the same script prepack uses rather than a second implementation.

steps.title: A doc that no check reads is a doc that can be missing while everything is green

axes.correctness: Every registry patch now has a docs/patches/P-NNNN-*.md. P-0016, the one that shipped without a doc, is written from the R24 record and checked against the code that shipped: the optional failureClasses and switchKey, the two governance tests, and the identical explain output. INDEX.md now names the real range instead of stopping at P-0015.
axes.reproducibility: The check was added before the missing doc was written and failed on the real state: FAIL registry/doc:P-0016. Writing the doc turns it green, and deleting the doc turns it red again; no fixture is needed because the repository already contained the failing case.
axes.compliance: The recovered doc follows the project format (symptom, measured, changed, limits, reproduction) and says it was written a round late rather than pretending it shipped with the patch. P-0023 is recorded tested, not verified, because a governance gate has no live artifact.
axes.ssot: The registry entry, the ledger row, the patch doc and the gate name the same paths; the snapshot is re-recorded after the registry change, and the ledger since is 0.4.1.
axes.adversarial: The adversary is the state that existed for five rounds: a patch in the registry with no doc, and a gate that only looked at evidence and guards. The check reads the filesystem per id, so an added patch without a doc is red on the next run rather than on the next audit.

steps.title: A page is outward text because of who reads it, not because of where it sits

axes.correctness: Both pages npm renders are now live manifest entries. gate_copy checks their bytes, fact-pack hash, prose numbers, placeholder and writer exactly as it does for the root README, and its covered list fails if either entry disappears. The bytes are the bytes that were already on disk; registering them was bookkeeping, not a rewrite.
axes.reproducibility: The registration was accepted by copy_record with zero unknown numbers, which is the same measurement P-0017 made. gate_copy prints covered:packages/plugin/README.md and covered:packages/core/README.md; deleting either entry from the manifest makes the gate red, and the negative control for the copy gate still corrupts a hash.
axes.compliance: The pages stay hand-written; this patch registers them instead of pretending to generate them. The P-0017 prose test remains as a second guard with a different criterion (no prose number at all, and every fenced command must be dispatchable), and its comment no longer claims gate_copy cannot see the pages.
axes.ssot: The registry entry, the ledger row, the patch doc and the manifest name the same two targets; the snapshot is re-recorded after the registry change, and the ledger since is 0.4.2 because 0.4.1 is already published.
axes.adversarial: The adversary is the state BS-13 described for five rounds: a page that is the first thing a stranger reads and is outside the channel that guards outward text. The covered list turns that state from "possible" into a red gate, and the number rule is the same one every other live entry is held to.

steps.title: A command that answers "is it on here" must not answer "off" when it was never asked

axes.correctness: Row.enabled became readonly string[] | null, where null means no profile was read. The cell prints unknown for null, (no) only for a read profile that switches every coverer off, and the coverer list otherwise. uncovered is incremented only when config !== null, so an unread profile can no longer produce exit 1. Measured before the fix: --sessions alone printed (no) and exited 1; after: unknown and exit 0, while repair:false still exits 1.
axes.reproducibility: tests/e2e/explain.test.ts grew three tests written before the fix; the first was red against the built CLI and the other two were already green, which is what keeps the finding path from being deleted rather than fixed. The session fixture is generated inside the test (one turn/end with MALFORMED_RESPONSE), so no host state is required.
axes.compliance: The package README, which npm renders, claimed the old semantics; it is a live copy entry, so the correction goes through copy_record and gate_copy rather than a hand edit. The patch is recorded tested, not verified, because the CLI has no resident seam to witness it. No byte cap was moved: the CLI half settled at 41362 of 42000 after the comments were condensed twice.
axes.ssot: The three-state vocabulary now lives in one place (the Row type and the printer) and the exit code uses EXIT_FINDING rather than a literal. The registry entry, the ledger row, the patch doc and the fact pack all name P-0025, and the doc quotes the same measured output the test asserts.
axes.adversarial: The adversary is the shape this project keeps finding: an unknown rendered as a value and then promoted into a finding. The middle test deliberately fails if the counting is removed, so the fix cannot be "make the exit code 0 by measuring nothing".

steps.title: A procedure with two homes rots in the one nobody reads, and that was the one the instructions pointed at

axes.correctness: docs/HANDOFF.md no longer restates the publish procedure: it points at docs/PUBLISH.md, and the boundary section no longer cites a .tmp/ tarball or a latest the packages do not ship. The three rules that enforce it were written first and all three failed against the recorded text.
axes.reproducibility: release-procedure.test.ts derives the supported flag set from scripts/publish_packages.mjs itself (process.argv.includes plus the flag helper) and pins it to --dry-run and --otp, so adding a flag to the script without naming it fails. Each rule carries an injected negative control in the same file; a rule that stops matching fails instead of passing quietly.
axes.compliance: The change edits documentation and adds one governance test; no emitted module changed, so the byte caps were not touched and the size gate is unchanged. The ledger, the registry entry and the patch doc were updated in the same round, and gate_registry now requires docs/patches/P-0026-*.md like every other patch.
axes.ssot: There is now one home for the release procedure. HANDOFF keeps the prohibition sentence (never put OTP, tokens or unredacted sessions in the repository) because that is a rule, not a procedure. The boundary section states versions the fact pack and the manifests also state, and the test compares its latest claim to the package version.
axes.adversarial: The adversary is the second copy that survived because handoff-truth only read two sections. The boundary rule refuses gitignored scratch paths specifically because a fresh clone cannot verify them, which is how that section kept saying 0.3.5 for four releases.
